evidence.V1: Front reads as a classic diamond (flat-topped crown over a pointed pavilion), top view as a clean elongated octagon, and the 3/4 silhouette as a gem. All three read at 64 px. The narrow end looks slightly rounded in the 3/4 outline, but it is still unmistakable.
evidence.V2: Big: crown and pavilion masses. Medium: a lighter table, a stepped ring of crown facets and the girdle band. Small: chamfer lines and corner facets. The table, crown and pavilion value steps make the tiers obvious.
evidence.V3: A confident chunky stylised gem: a tall stepped crown, a compact pavilion ending in a sharp-ish culet, and a footprint elongated about 0.95 x 0.80. It is not a stiff primitive. Symmetry error is X 0.0 / Y 0.0, the front outline is symmetric and the origin is centred.
evidence.V4: Even chamfers run along every crown step, the table rim and the girdle, and catch light as thin highlight lines in the studio close-ups. They are consistent across crown and pavilion, with no razor edges and nothing blobby.
evidence.V5: The close-ups (crown and pavilion, studio and flat) show crisp planar facets with no pinches, seams, z-fighting or overlapping caps. The gate shows A17/A18 pass, 0 flipped faces and 0 cap overlaps. Facet gradients come only from the one-sided Workbench light.
evidence.V6: One hue in three values: light table, mid crown, dark pavilion, as the kit intends. The colourways (crimson, royal) keep the same value structure.
evidence.V7: 286 tris against the small-class target of 600 (ceiling 1500), which is lean for a chamfered step-cut.
evidence.V8: One white material (LF_VertexColor, SmoothPlastic) with vertex colours, one hue in up to 3 values, chamfered edges with smooth shading. It sits beside the Coin_02 anchor without a visible clash.
evidence.V9: Studio line: Pickup with CanCollide off, CanTouch on, CollisionFidelity Box, Anchored, MeshPart.Color white for vertex colours, SmoothPlastic, origin at centre. All correct for a collectible.

artifacts: Minor: at the narrow ends of the octagon the small corner facets and chamfers blend into a soft gradient in the studio close-ups (crown close-up left end), so the facet edges read less crisply there. Not a defect.
Minor: the culet tip looks slightly blunted in the front and pavilion close-up views.
top_fixes: Sharpen the narrow-end corner facets (narrower chamfers or a slightly larger corner facet) so the step-cut stays crisp at the ends and the 3/4 outline reads less rounded.
Add a little more definition to the pavilion (for example a second tier of pavilion facets or a stronger value split) so the lower half carries the same detail density as the crown.
Bring the culet to a cleaner point so the front-view diamond silhouette ends crisply.
